title: C–G–Am–F Chord Change Drill
description: Practice four steady beats per chord at 72 BPM, with extra focus on the G-to-Am transition.
why: A metronome keeps the four-beat chord structure steady.
The fixed starting tempo supports clean repetitions before speeding up.
The repeated progression isolates the rushed G-to-Am change.
instructions: Set your metronome to 72 BPM. Play C for 4 beats, G for 4, Am for 4, and F for 4, then repeat. Count aloud and prepare the next chord during beat 4 without rushing. Complete 3 clean repetitions; only then raise the tempo by 4 BPM. If you stumble, return to 72 BPM.
